title: A laptop reaches the memory service and the dispatcher on a shared cluster
why: On a shared, managed cluster there is no load balancer the owner's machine can use, so sessions there have neither memory nor messages.
takes: Decide the way in (the cluster's own ingress with its identity, or a tunnel), then make the chart and the laptop's settings take it. Needs a shared cluster to try on.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "the way in from a laptop to a service on a shared cluster"
ADR 0049, What would make us look again: "A shared cluster with no load balancer the machine can reach: the way in from a laptop to a service on a shared cluster is not built for the memory either."

title: Each machine of the owner's is a place of its own
why: A second machine would share the first one's place, token and session names, and needs copies of the owner's token and of the dispatcher's settings by hand.
takes: A place and a host token per machine in the values and the secret; the deploy script writes each machine's settings.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "more than one machine of the owner's (one place per installation)"
ADR 0049, Consequences: "One place per installation. A second machine would share the place and its token, and its sessions' names with it."
ADR 0051, Consequences: "A second machine of the owner's needs a copy of the file"

title: A session on the owner's machine whose harness died is known to be gone, and opened again for a message
why: A session closed without its end hook looks running for up to a day, and a message for it waits for the next session of its name with nobody told.
takes: Run `dispatcher attend` on the machine with the place's token; opening a session again needs a terminal the person will look at, which the machine's configuration provides.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "the watcher of ADR 0053 on the owner's machine"
ADR 0053, The owner's machine (not built)
ADR 0049, Consequences: "A session on the machine that the owner closes without SessionEnd (a killed terminal) looks running for up to a day"

title: The task-stream benchmark says whether memory is useful (M7)
why: M7 is the requirement the memory exists for, and it is checked only in its smallest form, by the transfer benchmark.
takes: A fixed sequence of tasks, a fresh session each, only memory carried over, graded by scripts; arms as DESIGN section 7 lists them.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "the task-stream benchmark (M7)"
DESIGN.md section 7: "Task stream (not built)"

title: A second harness completes the benchmark with only the CLI (M8)
why: M8 says memory is modular; nothing but Claude Code has used it.
takes: Run the carman arm of the benchmark on another harness that has a shell.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "a second harness (M8)"

title: An agent's work is started by a webhook or a ticket, not only by the clock or a message
why: R2 asks for triggers that are many to many; today work starts on a schedule, by hand, or by a message.
takes: An endpoint of the dispatcher that turns a signed request into an event, and a rule from events to tasks. A design first: what authenticates a caller from outside.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "for agents that do work outside memory: triggers other than a schedule"
REQUIREMENTS.md R2: "A task can be started by a webhook and by a schedule"

title: The owner answers an agent's message where the notice arrives
why: A notice is one-way: to answer, the owner goes to a machine that reaches the cluster and runs `dispatch reply`, so answers come late or not at all.
takes: The installation's notice channel carries a reply back as a message that answers the one the notice was about; what proves the reply is the owner's has to be decided.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "a way for the owner to answer an agent's message where it arrives (today: dispatch reply from the laptop)"
ADR 0036, Decision: "A reply in the chat does not reach the agent. Not built."

title: Every scheduled agent is started by the dispatcher
why: Agents still started by the cluster's own schedules are not held by admission, so pacing cannot place their work; their missed runs are only noticed after the fact.
takes: One agent at a time: `dispatched: true` on its entry, a run watched through, then the next. No code is expected, only what the first moves show is missing.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "The scheduled agents are not yet moved onto the dispatcher"
ADR 0043, Consequences: "it acts only on tasks the dispatcher starts: the scheduled agents still on CronJobs are not held"

title: Backlog work is paced by a curve that reaches full at the window's reset
why: R7: unused capacity at reset should stay under a target, and a fixed threshold either starves backlog work or lets it eat the owner's headroom.
takes: Replace the threshold in admission by expected use at reset; emit an event saying how much of which window is expected to go unused, which the improvement loop's gate then reads in place of its own rule.
evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Not built yet": "pacing is a threshold, not yet a curve to the window's reset"
ADR 0058: the gate's rule for room in usage is a stand-in until this exists

title: The dreamer can be written to and can write, as agents can
why: The dreamer's questions for the owner go through a notice and a resumed conversation; it has no token for the dispatcher and no label a message could start it by.
takes: Give the dreamer's pod the projected token and the label, and decide what a restricted routine may do with messages.
evidence: ADR 0045, Consequences: "The dreamer's pod has neither yet: it can neither message nor be messaged."

title: Something limits how many runs a session can start by writing messages
why: A message to an agent by name, or to a session that is not running, costs a run of that agent's model; a confused session can start many.
takes: A count per sender and day in the dispatcher's send, with a refusal that says so; the number in the values.
evidence: ADR 0045, Consequences: "Nothing limits how many messages a session sends but the running limit."

title: REQUIREMENTS.md has a requirement for messages between sessions, agents and the owner
why: Messaging is built and tested against R2 only; the owner asked that it be no worse than the harness's own, and nothing states that as a check.
takes: The owner adds the wording ADR 0045 proposes (R11), or other wording; the tests then name it. Only the owner edits that file.
evidence: ADR 0045, Consequences: "Proposed wording for the owner to add, if wanted: R11 | Sessions, agents and the owner can write to each other | A message reaches its addressee whether its session is busy, idle or not running, once; the sender can see what became of it."

title: R9, human approval gates, is written
why: R9 has been open since the first version, 'to be written after observing unattended runs'. The improvement loop is the first thing that starts work by itself and has a gate; ADR 0058 proposes wording from it.
takes: The owner writes R9, from ADR 0058's proposal or otherwise.
evidence: REQUIREMENTS.md R9: "Open. To be written after observing unattended runs"
ADR 0058, Proposed wording for R9

title: A notice that carries an identifier or a secret-shaped string is caught before it is sent
why: The notice channel is not private; what goes into a notice is the agent's judgement and nothing checks it. The memory service already refuses credential-shaped strings.
takes: Run the memory's secret check over a notice's words in `notify-owner`'s caller or in the dispatcher's notice task, and withhold with a reason on a hit.
evidence: ADR 0048, Consequences: "What is personal or an identifier is the agent's judgement, for what it writes itself; nothing checks it."

title: The proxy refuses model calls of an agent that is over its budget
why: A run's budget is the harness's own stop; the proxy's meter counts what each agent used and enforces nothing.
takes: A budget per agent and period in the values, read by the meter; a refusal the harness shows as a limit. An event per request, if a budget needs it.
evidence: ADR 0050, Consequences: "Not built: a budget the proxy enforces, and an event for each request."

title: The account's usage is read from the model's answers as they pass the proxy
why: The hourly reading costs a call per model and is up to six hours old for most models, while every answer the proxy passes carries the windows.
takes: The meter records the rate-limit headers of answers as `usage.observed`; the hourly reading stays for hours with no traffic.
evidence: ADR 0050, Consequences: "The hourly reading could be read from the answers' headers instead; not done."
ADR 0052, Consequences: "A model read every six hours can be refused for up to six hours before the status says so"

title: The model's credential is only at the proxy, and the switch that puts it back in pods is gone
why: `pod` and `both` keep a path on which every agent pod holds the credential; ADR 0050 says when they can go.
takes: After a month through the meter with no request failed by it and no unexplained disagreement: remove the two modes and mount the credential only in the meter.
evidence: ADR 0050, "When the switch can go"

title: The shapes of a usage refusal are checked against a real refusal
why: The reading's parsing of a refused call was written from the harness's schema and tested on made-up lines; if it is wrong, admission holds or admits on a misreading.
takes: At the first real refusal, compare the recorded event with the parser's expectations and add it to the tests.
evidence: ADR 0052, Consequences: "the first real refusal should be checked against them"

title: Admission knows the model a routine will really start with
why: A dreamer routine with a ladder of its own is admitted or held by the default ladder's first model, which may not be the one it runs.
takes: Read the routine's own ladder from the job template's environment where the task names its routine.
evidence: ADR 0052, Consequences: "a dreamer routine's own ladder (CMEM_ROUTINE_MODELS_NAME) is not read, only the default one"

title: An agent in a trial installation can reach the model
why: A change to a routine or to how agents run cannot be tried end to end in a trial; the improvement loop's own routine was tried from a session's pod instead.
takes: The installation's proxy takes callers from the sandbox and names them `trial` in its record, behind a value (ADR 0054 prefers this to a credential in the sandbox).
evidence: ADR 0054, Not in the first version: "A trial agent that reaches the model."
ADR 0058, What was tried: the routine could not run as an agent of the trial

title: Two agents of a trial write to each other
why: Messaging between agents is tried in a trial only with pods made by hand for the purpose.
takes: Agent definitions in the trial's values and pods with the projected token; no model is needed to send and read.
evidence: ADR 0054, Not in the first version: "Messages between two trial agents."
ADR 0058: scripts/check-improve.sh makes stand-in pods by hand for this reason

title: Two sessions can each have a trial at the same time
why: A trial keeps the chart's names, so a namespace holds one; a second session waits for the first to take its trial down, and nothing tells it when.
takes: Either a name prefix the deploy script and chart both take, or a sandbox namespace per session; ADR 0054 chose the chart's names so that the scripts are tried as they are.
evidence: ADR 0054, Decision: "One trial at a time in one namespace."
2026-11-27, building ADR 0058: `trial.sh up` refused because another session's trial was in the sandbox, and waited

title: The registry lets go of the images of trials that are over
why: Every `trial.sh up` of a changed checkout leaves two images that nothing removes.
takes: A retention on the registry by name pattern, or a clean-up job of the installation's: nothing in the sandbox may delete from it.
evidence: ADR 0054, Consequences: "The registry keeps the trial's images after down: nothing in the sandbox may delete from it."

title: An agent can be limited to named commands, as the dreamer is
why: The surveyor of the improvement loop needs one command (`dispatcher improve`) and runs with every tool, because only the dreamer takes command prefixes from the chart and the test for a prefix admits only verbs that read.
takes: Let an agent's entry name command prefixes, and decide what test replaces 'plainly a read' for a command that writes on purpose.
evidence: ADR 0046, Consequences: "Only the dreamer takes them from the chart."
ADR 0058, Consequences: the surveyor runs with tools: all

title: The surveyor reads what the dreamer could not check
why: The dreamer's nightly report lists what it could not check or had to ask; it is in the run's kept conversation and its log, not in the dispatcher's log, so the improvement loop does not see it.
takes: The routine runner records a routine's last words as an event (`run.report`), and the evidence includes it under the same rule as messages.
evidence: ADR 0058, Not in the first version

title: A plain go build works in an agent's pod
why: The agent image has no C compiler, so `go build` and `go vet` fail until CGO_ENABLED=0 is set; scripts/test.sh sets it, a session's own first build does not, and each new session finds this out again.
takes: Set CGO_ENABLED=0 in the agent image's environment.
evidence: 2026-11-27, building ADR 0058 in a platform session's pod: `go build ./...` ended with: cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found: exec: "gcc": executable file not found in $PATH
